record.original_question: For any graph G, do the coefficients of its chromatic polynomial always form an infinitely log-concave sequence, not merely a log-concave one?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 13.1. The coefficients of any chromatic polynomial form infinitely log-concave sequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with n vertices, and let χ_G(k) denote its chromatic polynomial, which counts the number of proper colorings of G using k colors. Write
  χ_G(k) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^{n−i} a_i(G) k^i,
so that a_0(G), a_1(G), …, a_n(G) are nonnegative integers (the absolute values of the coefficients of χ_G).

For a finite sequence of nonnegative real numbers s = (s_0, s_1, …, s_n), define the operator L by
  (L s)_i = s_i^2 − s_{i−1} s_{i+1},   for 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1,
with (L s)_0 = s_0^2 and (L s)_n = s_n^2. The sequence s is called log-concave if L s has all nonnegative entries. It is called infinitely log-concave (or ∞-log-concave) if L^m s has all nonnegative entries for every integer m ≥ 1.

Question: Is it true that for every finite simple graph G, the sequence (a_0(G), a_1(G), …, a_n(G)) of absolute values of coefficients of the chromatic polynomial of G is infinitely log-concave?
artifact.status_search_result: Ordinary log-concavity of the coefficients of the chromatic polynomial (Read–Hoggar / Rota–Heron–Welsh) was established by Huh and subsequently extended in the matroid setting by Adiprasito–Huh–Katz and others. However, no proof of the stronger statement that these coefficient sequences are infinitely (∞-)log-concave has been located; the strengthened conjecture appears to remain open, with infinite log-concavity verified only in special cases or for related sequences.

status_evidence.title: Milnor numbers of projective hypersurfaces and the chromatic polynomial of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Huh proves log-concavity of the coefficients of the chromatic polynomial, settling the Read conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Single log-concavity of chromatic polynomial coefficients is proven, but not the stronger infinite log-concavity.

status_evidence.title: On Multiple and Infinite Log-Concavity (Medina–Straub)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the notion of ∞-log-concavity and lists open problems; verifies infinite log-concavity in various special families.
status_evidence.claim: Infinite log-concavity is studied separately and remains open in many natural cases including chromatic polynomials.

status_evidence.title: The log-concavity of chromatic polynomials (Hollebenthiago, MSc)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of log-concavity results for chromatic polynomials, with no statement of an infinite log-concavity proof.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of infinite log-concavity is reported.
